content: Before taking demeclocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, or to other tetracycline medications such as doxycycline, minocycline, or tetracycline, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are sure you can perform them safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Demeclocycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication can also increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used in children under 8 years of age as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using demeclocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some urine tests for sugar, potentially causing false test results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. If this medication is used for long-term treatment or to manage SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion), regular lab and/or medical tests (such as complete blood count, kidney/liver function, and mineral levels) should be performed. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated demeclocycline can result in serious illness. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually 2 to 4 times a day. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this drug. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (such as milk and yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For the best effect, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced times. If you are taking this medication to treat an infection, continue to take it until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Common side effects may include diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or rectal discomfort. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Tetracycline drugs, such as demeclocycline, may rarely cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension, or IH). The risk of this side effect is higher in women of childbearing age who are overweight or have had IH in the past. If IH develops, it usually resolves after stopping demeclocycline; however, there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
